Pfingsten’s American Cutting Edge Acquires Pilot Precision Products

American Cutting Edge, a portfolio company of Pfingsten, acquired Pilot Precision Products. The deal closed on Oct. 30, 2026. It is ACE’s first acquisition under Pfingsten’s ownership and Pfingsten’s 121st add-on.

Pilot makes and distributes broaches, cutting tools and precision drill bits, the replaceable tooling manufacturers use to cut and drill parts. Based in South Deerfield, Massachusetts, it serves industrial, aerospace and defense, medical, electronics and equipment customers. ACE distributes consumable knives, blades and razors and provides sharpening, etching and inventory management for customers in recycling, converting, flooring installation, plastics, food and packaging, tree care and archery. Scott Finegan, senior managing director at Pfingsten, said Pilot’s customer relationships and industry expertise make it a valuable addition to the ACE platform. Chicago-based Pfingsten has raised six funds with about $1.8 billion of commitments.

Cortec Group Sells A1 Garage Door Service to KKR

Cortec Group sold A1 Garage Door Service to KKR. Cortec made the sale through its affiliate Cortec Group Fund VII, which partnered with A1 in December 2022.

A1 repairs and replaces garage doors for homeowners, using its own employed technicians and installers across 29 geographies. Founder and CEO Tommy Mello will continue to lead the business and keep a significant ownership stake. Under Cortec, A1 expanded through new locations and add-on acquisitions, grew its technician and installer team, built out its management group, centralized technician training and put AI-enabled technology to work in customer acquisition, call center operations and dispatch. Doug Kruep, a managing partner at Cortec, said the firm saw an opportunity to help A1 grow organically and through acquisitions. Piper Sandler was lead financial advisor to A1, with William Blair as co-advisor and Paul Hastings as legal counsel.

Skyline Investors Backs $10 Million-Plus Club Reinvestment at YouFit Gyms

Skyline Investors, a Los Angeles private equity firm, has made a $10 million-plus investment in YouFit Gyms to fund a reinvestment in the gym operator’s existing clubs. The first phase covers 12 club refreshes across Florida, starting with South Florida clubs in December 2026. The deal is Skyline’s first investment in fitness and wellness.

YouFit runs low-cost gyms that give members access to equipment, training and fitness guidance at an affordable price. Founded in 2008 and based in Deerfield Beach, Florida, it operates 49 clubs in four states. The refreshes will add new workout floors and equipment, expanded strength areas, recovery offerings and more functional training areas. Jason Carter, who became chief executive in April 2026, said the investment will strengthen YouFit’s value for current and future members. Jeremy May, founder and managing partner of Skyline, said the firm plans to help YouFit expand recovery and longevity services in its communities.

Legacy Star’s Peak 10 Energy Secures $500 Million Acquisition Facility from U.S. Bank

Peak 10 Energy, a portfolio company of Legacy Star Capital Partners, has secured an acquisition finance facility of up to $500 million from U.S. Bank. The facility will fund purchases of oil and gas asset packages across the U.S., primarily proved developed producing properties, and is structured to support later asset-backed securities issuances as a long-term financing source.

Peak 10 Energy acquires and develops producing oil and gas properties, focusing on long-life assets with steady cash flow. Based in Houston and founded in 2023, it holds operated, non-operated and mineral positions in U.S. onshore basins and has closed 12 acquisition and divestiture transactions. Kyle McQuire, chief executive, said the facility, together with a commodity hedging relationship with U.S. Bank, gives the company capital to buy assets at greater scale. Petrie Partners originated the transaction and served as financial advisor to Peak 10, with Baker Botts as legal counsel. Haynes Boone advised U.S. Bank.

Washington Harbour’s Trusted Space Acquires Falcon ExoDynamics

Trusted Space, a portfolio company of Washington Harbour Partners, has acquired Falcon ExoDynamics, an El Segundo, California developer of spacecraft autonomy technology. Washington Harbour made a strategic growth investment in Trusted Space in 2025.

Falcon ExoDynamics builds the onboard software and hardware that let spacecraft operate and maneuver on their own. Founded in 2017, it provides spacecraft-level autonomy, rendezvous and proximity operations, mission engineering and integrated payload products for aerospace companies and government customers. Trusted Space, founded in 2019, makes mission autonomy and battlespace management software for defense and intelligence customers. The combination pairs Falcon’s vehicle-level autonomy with Trusted Space’s mission-level software, with applications in battle management command and control and maneuvering operations in orbit. Robert MacMillan, president and chief executive of Trusted Space, said the combined company aims to deliver autonomy operators can trust, from a single spacecraft to full constellations.

Berkshire Partners’ United Flow Technologies Adds Envirolutions

United Flow Technologies, a portfolio company of Berkshire Partners, has added Envirolutions to its group of regional brands, expanding its presence in the Northeast.

Envirolutions helps municipal water and wastewater utilities choose, install and maintain the equipment that keeps their treatment systems running. Founded in 1999 by Ralph Tingler, it represents manufacturers of pumps, mixers, blowers, filtration equipment, screens and drives, and supports customers from equipment selection through service and aftermarket parts across the New York metropolitan area and northern New Jersey. Irving, Texas-based UFT is a technical distributor of process equipment for municipal and industrial water and wastewater markets. Matt Hart, chief executive of UFT, said the deal advances the company’s plan to build a technical platform for municipal water and wastewater one regional brand at a time. The Envirolutions founder said UFT shares its focus on service and long-term partnerships.

Butterfly Equity’s Actus Nutrition Acquires Erie Foods’ North American Operations

Actus Nutrition, a portfolio company of Butterfly Equity, has acquired the North American operations of Erie Foods International. The transaction closed on October 26, 2026. Erie Europe was excluded from the sale and will operate independently. PKF Investment Banking served as exclusive financial advisor to Erie Foods.

Erie Foods makes the dairy proteins that food, nutraceutical and supplement companies build into their products. Founded in 1938 by the Reisenbigler family and based in Erie, Illinois, it produces caseins, caseinates, milk protein crisps, concentrates and isolates, and provides custom processing including twin-screw extrusion, agglomeration, drying, blending and particle coating. Eden Prairie, Minnesota-based Actus converts milk and whey into functional ingredients for human and animal nutrition. David Lenzmeier, chief executive of Actus, said Erie adds complementary capabilities that broaden its protein ingredient offerings.

Oak Hill’s Petauri Acquires Emotive

Petauri, a pharmaceutical services platform backed by Oak Hill Capital, has acquired medical communications agency Emotive. Emotive joins Petauri Advance, Petauri’s medical communications group, alongside agencies including DRIVE, PROPEL, MOMENTUM, BluPrint Oncology, Verascity Science and Cogency.

Emotive helps pharmaceutical and life sciences companies explain the science behind their medicines to the healthcare professionals who care for patients. Founded in 2013, it works in neuroscience and immunology as well as oncology and rare disease, from offices in London and Boston. Founder and CEO Chris Edmonds will serve as an executive adviser within the organization. Petauri CEO Dan Renick said clients need partners who understand the science and can translate it for those who shape patient care. Nashville-based Petauri has more than 600 professionals in market access and scientific communications, and Oak Hill plans to invest more than $250 million of equity from its OHCP VI fund in the platform.

Coalesce’s Marshall & Stevens Acquires Baumann Moreau

Marshall & Stevens, a valuation, litigation support and transaction advisory firm owned by Coalesce Capital, has acquired Baumann Moreau, a forensic accounting firm in Tampa, Florida. The deal expands Marshall & Stevens’ litigation support practice in Florida and adds referral channels across its valuation service lines.

Baumann Moreau examines financial records and serves as an expert witness for parties in civil, commercial and family litigation, and it also values businesses. Founders Paul Baumann and Leslie Moreau started the firm in 2007. Marshall & Stevens CEO Nishen Radia said litigation support is strategically important to the firm and that the deal strengthens its presence in an attractive market. Founded in 1932 and based in Los Angeles, Marshall & Stevens serves clients in energy and infrastructure, healthcare, manufacturing, financial services and real estate. New York-based Coalesce invests in human capital-driven and technology-enabled services companies and has more than $1.8 billion in regulatory assets under management.

Arcline Sells Akron Bio to MaxCyte for $151.8 Million

Arcline Investment Management has agreed to sell Akron Bio to MaxCyte (Nasdaq: MXCT) for $151.8 million. The consideration comprises $105 million in cash, about 20.6 million MaxCyte shares valued at roughly $26.8 million, and $20 million in guaranteed deferred payments due in January 2028 and January 2029. Closing is expected before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.

Akron Bio makes GMP-grade reagents and ancillary materials that cell therapy developers use to manufacture their treatments. Founded in 2006 and based in Boca Raton, Florida, it will continue to operate under its own brand and is expected to generate about $28 million of revenue and $7 million to $8 million of EBITDA in 2026. MaxCyte, of Rockville, Maryland, makes electroporation instruments and consumables used to engineer cells, and expects the deal to nearly double its revenue base. Arcline acquired a majority interest in Akron in 2019.

Five Point Infrastructure Sells Deep Blue Midland Basin Stake to Diamondback and KKR

Five Point Infrastructure has agreed to sell its majority interest in Deep Blue Midland Basin, a produced-water infrastructure company in Texas, to Diamondback Energy, already a minority owner, and KKR. The sale is for cash. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions.

Deep Blue gathers, transports, stores, treats, recycles and disposes of the water that comes up with oil and gas production in the Midland Basin. Based in The Woodlands and Midland, Texas, it was formed in 2023 as a joint venture between Five Point and Diamondback. It manages more than 2.2 million barrels of water per day, including recycling, with more than 2,000 miles of pipeline and 142 million barrels of storage. David Capobianco, CEO and managing partner of Five Point, said the firm saw a growing need for water management in the basin when Deep Blue was founded. Houston-based Five Point invests in North American water management, surface management, powered land and sustainable infrastructure and has more than $10 billion in assets under management.
